Award/Judgment Factual Position And Pleadings
1. A Dar was filed on 21.03.2023 by the Investigating Officer and registered on 28.03.2023.

The
said Dar was related to a motor vehicular accident dated 18.12.2022 at a
bout 09.00 AM
in which one Anuj S/o Sh. Santosh (hereinafter referred to as "petitioner") sustained injuries.

As per mother of petitioner, at the relevant date, her son namely Anuj (aged about 06 years) alongwith their neighbour Babulal's son namely Anshu and daughter Anshika were standing on the footpath in front of Leelawati School and they were making fire by burning wood and she was present on the footpath on the side of her jhuggi and at about 09.00 AM, a white Brezza car bearing no.
DL-9CAX-4489(hereinafter referred to as PANKAJ Date:
SHARMA 2024.10.08 16:02:39 +0530 "offending vehicle") driving by its driver(herein R-1) came from Leelawati School at a high speed, carelessness and negligently and hit the children who were sitting on the footpath except the Anshika as she saved herself by turning aside.
However, her son Anuj and neighbour's son Anshu got injured in the collision and suffered grievous injuries.

After the collision,
driver came down from car and on inquiry, he told his name as Gajender Singh S/o Sh. Mahipal Singh.
Her son Anuj was picked up by her sister's son Vinod and took him to Hospital and their neighbour Kishori took Anshu to Deep Chand Bandhu Hospital.

An FIR bearing no. 323/2022, U/s. 279/338 IPC & 3/181, 5/180 M.V. Act,
PS Gulabi Bagh has been registered against the driver of the offending vehicle.
R-1 is the driver and R-2 is owner of the offending vehicle.
R-3 is stated to be the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Respondents were directed to file their Written Statements.

PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA

I have perused the record and my issue wise findings is as under:-
ISSUE NO.1 "Whether the petitioner Anuj suffered injuries in an accident that took place on 18.12.2022 at about 09:00 AM involving vehicle bearing registration No.
DL-9CAX- 4489 driven by the Respondent No. 1 rashly and negligently, owned by the respondent no. 2 and insured with the respondent no. 3?

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

However, her son Anuj and neighbour's son Anshu got injured in the collision and suffered grievous injuries.

After the collision,
R-1 came down from car and on inquiry, he told his name as Gajender Singh S/o Sh. Mahipal Singh.
Her son Anuj was picked up by her sister's son Vinod and took him to Hospital and their neighbour Kishori took Anshu to Deep Chand Bandhu Hospital.

Petitioner claimed compensation on account of special pecuniary damage relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicine, transportation, diet,
loss of earning during the period, he was injured, loss of earning during the period of treatment,
future medical expenses, non-pecuniary damages, damages for pain suffering and trauma, loss of amenities, loss of expectation of life alongwith interest.

Further, there is nothing on record which betrays any falsity or untruth in the oral testimony of PANKAJ Date:
SHARMA 2024.10.08 16:03:03 +0530 PW-1.
As such, it could be safely held that the oral testimony of PW-1 is reliable and trustworthy.

12. The very fact that R-1 has already been chargesheeted for the offences punishable under Sections 279/338 IPC and 3/181 & 5/180 of M.V. Act in the above criminal case/FIR in itself is a strong circumstance to support the above oral testimony of PW1 and the case of petitioner on this issue.

The copies of FIR, Chargesheet, Site plan, Mechanical inspection report of offending vehicle, MLC,
arrest and Seizure Memos of R-1 also corroborate the testimony of PW1.
13.

Besides the above, R-1 himself was the best witness who could have stepped into the witness box to challenge the depositions being made by PW1 regarding the above accident and its manner etc.,
but he has not done so.

Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.

The same is duly substantiated by the site plan.

In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
15. In view of the MLC and medical treatment documents placed on record by the petitioner, no dispute is left regarding the nature of injuries sustained by him in the above accident.

16. In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal holds that the petitioner suffered grievous injuries on his person on account of negligence and default of R-1 while driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
This issue thus stands decided against the respondents and in favour of the petitioner.

PANKAJ Date:
SHARMA 2024.10.08 16:03:09 +0530 "Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?

If so, to what amount and from whom?"
17.

As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
18. In terms of provisions contained in Section 168 of the MV Act the compensation which is to be awarded by this tribunal is required to be 'just'.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.

The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The "non-pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.

The pecuniary or special damages generally include the expenses incurred by the claimant towards his treatment, special diet, conveyance, cost of nursing/ attendant, loss of income/earning capacity etc.
and the non-pecuniary damages generally include the PANKAJ Date:
SHARMA 2024.10.08 16:03:13 +0530 compensation for the mental or physical shock, pain and sufferings, loss of amenities of life, marriage prospects and disfiguration etc.
The above categories falling under both the heads of compensation are not exhaustive in nature but only illustrative.

It is also necessary to state here that no amount of money or compensation can put the injured/claimant exactly in the Anuj (I) (Fir 323/2022/Gulabi Bagh) vs Gajender (The New India) on 8 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60909787/

The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.

It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.

Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited, (2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.

In light of the above legal propositions, the amount of compensation which can be considered to be 'just' in the opinion of this Tribunal shall be as under:-
PANKAJ SHARMA SHARMA Date:
2024.10.08 16:03:16 +0530 (i) Medical or Treatment Expenses 20.
Although, the petitioner has not placed on record any medical bills but a pragmatic view is required to be taken considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner.
Petitioner has averred that he has incurred about Rs.1,00,000/-, however, there is no document which can substantiate the same.
Therefore, keeping in view the nature of injuries, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- under this head.
(ii) Pain and Suffering 21.
As per MLC and medical record filed on behalf of the petitioner, the petitioner suffered grievous injury.

In chargesheet, R- 1 namely Gajender was challaned u/s. 279/338 IPC & 3/181, 5/180 M.V.
Act.

It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the pain and sufferings which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.

Hence, keeping in view the extent and nature of the injuries suffered by petitioner and duration of the treatment taken by him etc., an amount of Rs.35,000/- is liable to be awarded to him towards pain and sufferings.
Thus, he is awarded a total amount of Rs.35,000/- under this head.
(iii) Loss of studies 22.
In affidavit Ex. PW1/A, mother of petitioner claims that the petitioner Anuj was 6 years old and was studying in 1 st standard.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.
The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.
Reference in this regard can be made to the propositions of law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Bimla Devi and others Vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also recently in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd. & Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.
Therefore, an adverse inference on this aspect is also required to be drawn against the respondents in view of the law laid down in case of Cholamandalam M.S. General Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh, reported in 2009 (3) AD (Delhi) 310.
14.
In view of the above, it could be safely assumed that at the relevant date and time, her son namely Anuj alongwith their neighbour Babulal's son namely Anshu and daughter Anshika were standing on the footpath in front of Leelawati School and they were making fire by burning wood and she was present on the footpath on PANKAJ SHARMA Date:
However, her son Anuj and neighbour's son Anshu got injured in the collision and suffered grievous injuries.
In the absence of any averment or evidence regarding any mechanical defect in the offending vehicle or any material depicting any negligent/sudden act or omission on the part of the petitioner, the only inference possible in the given facts and circumstances is that of neglect and default on the part of R-1 in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
In view of the above discussion, this Tribunal is constrained to hold R-1 guilty of gross negligence and default in driving the offending vehicle at the relevant time.
As the issue no.1 has been proved in affirmative and in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner has become entitled to be compensated for the injuries suffered in the above accident, but the computation of compensation and liability to pay the same are required to be decided.
In the injury cases a claimant is entitled to two different kinds of compensations i.e. Pecuniary as well as non- pecuniary damages.
The "pecuniary damages" or special damages are those damages which are awarded and designed to make good the losses which are capable of being calculated in terms of money and the object of awarding these damages is to indemnify the claimant for the expenses which he had already incurred or is likely to incur in respect of the injuries suffered by him in the accident.
The "non-pecuniary" or general damages are those damages which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations.
same position or place where he was before the accident and an effort is to be made only to reasonably compensate him or to put him almost in the same place or position where he could have been if the alleged accident had not taken place and this compensation is to be assessed in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner.
The object of compensating him is also not to reward him or to make him rich in an unjust manner.
It is also well settled that the 'just' compensation to be awarded to the claimant has to be calculated objectively and it may involve some guess work in calculating the different amounts which the claimant may be entitled under the different heads of compensation.
Reference in this regard can be made on some of important judgments on the subject like the judgment in the case of R.D. Hattangadi Vs. Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., AIR 1995 SC 755, Arvind Kumar Mishra Vs. New India Assurance Company Limited, (2010) 10 SCC 254 and Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr., (2011) 1 SCC 343.
19.
Although, the petitioner has not placed on record any medical bills but a pragmatic view is required to be taken considering the nature of injuries suffered by the petitioner.
As per MLC and medical record filed on behalf of the petitioner, the petitioner suffered grievous injury.
It is not possible to quantify the compensation admissible to petitioner for the pain and sufferings which he actually suffered because of the above injuries, but as stated above, an effort has to be made to compensate him for the same in a just and reasonable manner.
After receiving amendments in the MV Act, the concept of pay and recover has done away with.
As per the facts, the R-1 was not holding a valid and effective driving license at the time of accident and has committed the breach of contract of insurance policy.
